title: China, Sri Lanka and the United States: reserves, current, capital and financial accounts, GDP, consumer prices and the exchange rate, annual, 1982-2025
source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (API v2); the balance-of-payments series come from the IMF's Balance of Payments Statistics and International Financial Statistics
series: FI.RES.TOTL.CD (reserves: total reserves including gold, current US$); BN.CAB.XOKA.CD (ca: current account balance, BoP, current US$); BN.FIN.TOTL.CD (fa: net financial account, BoP, current US$); BN.RES.INCL.CD (res_bop: reserves and related items, BoP, current US$); NY.GDP.MKTP.CD (gdp, current US$); BN.TRF.KOGT.CD (ka: net capital account, current US$); FP.CPI.TOTL (cpi: consumer price index, 2010 = 100); PA.NUS.FCRF (fx: official exchange rate, LCU per US$, period average)
license: CC BY-4.0 (the 'License_Type' of every series in the WDI metadata, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/sources/2/series/<code>/metadata, 2026-10-14)
citation: World Bank, World Development Indicators (last updated 2026-10-08).
notes: WDI last updated 2026-10-08. Signs follow BPM6: fa is net lending (net acquisition of financial assets less net incurrence of liabilities), positive when residents add more to their foreign assets than to their foreign liabilities; res_bop is the transaction in reserve assets, positive when reserves rise. Net errors and omissions = fa - ca - ka. Values revise with each WDI release; the IMF's and the national compilers' later revisions make some years differ from the figures first published (e.g. SAFE's 2016 report gave China's 2016 current account as 196.4 billion; WDI now has 191.3).
